title: 1973 Greater London Council election
summary: Labour, led by Reg Goodwin, won a large majority of 58 of the 92 seats, ending six years of Conservative control. The Liberals won their first ever GLC seats, taking two. The election was the first fought in 92 single-member divisions matching the parliamentary constituencies, and saw a young Ken Livingstone elected for Lambeth, Norwood.
highlights: Labour returns to power with 58 of 92 seats
The Liberals win their first two GLC seats on 12.5% of the vote
First election using 92 single-member constituency divisions
Ken Livingstone first elected to the GLC

council.note: From 1973 the GLC was elected from 92 single-member divisions coterminous with the Greater London parliamentary constituencies, replacing the earlier borough-based multi-member areas.
